- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75–80 range), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture the “rebound” or “mean reversion” after peaks.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the final 10–15 days of the 30-day forecast, especially when true values are trending lower.
- Model often fails to adjust for seasonal or cyclical mean reversion — overestimates when prices are near historical highs, underestimates when near lows.
- Forecasts show lag in responding to recent price drops — model takes 2–3 days to “catch up” to true trend, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates sharp downward moves, overestimates gradual declines.
- When true values are below 60, model often overcorrects upward, suggesting it’s “fearing” a drop and overcompensating.
- Model is sensitive to recent history — if last 5–7 days are high, model overestimates; if recent days are low, model underestimates — exhibits “memory bias.”
